findings.detail: SelectNearest_EqualDistance_DeterministicTiebreak asserts only resultA.DriverId == resultB.DriverId (determinism across input order), never that the winner is id1 (the smaller GUID). Any deterministic tiebreak direction, including descending, passes this assertion, so it does not pin the documented ascending ThenBy(DriverId) direction. It also relies on the two haversine distances (PickupLng +/- 0.01) being bit-identical via FP odd-symmetry; if they ever diverge by 1 ULP, OrderBy(Distance) alone fixes the winner and ThenBy is never the deciding factor, so the tie-path stops being exercised.

MakeCandidate declares lat and lng parameters that are dead: every caller relies on the driverLat/driverLng fallthrough and never passes lat/lng, and the null-position test bypasses the helper entirely by constructing DriverCandidate directly. Unused helper parameters.
